Eight distinct directions, each with a front and back. Made from your website’s exact colors, Danfo lettering, and flower-farm personality. Tap the hearts to keep a shortlist.

01

Pink tide

The signature choice. Big pink energy, the site’s rolling wave, and a punchy plum reverse.

02

The growers seal

Quiet, warm, and personal. The original daisy-and-hatchet illustration becomes a small farm seal.

03

After dark

A graphic, music-poster attitude. Deep plum and acid green give this one the sharpest edge.

04

In full bloom

A miniature portfolio. The homepage bouquet brings real flowers and rich photographic texture into the hand.

05

Flower power

An unabashedly playful lavender-and-pink daisy repeat, with a cream oval wordmark and social-first reverse.

06

Field notes

Earthier and more restrained. Olive, fine rules, and a blush illustration panel feel like an elegant farm label.

07

Pocket garden

A portrait keepsake. One oversized daisy grows between the brand and the Pacifica sign-off.

08

The sharp cut

A bold diagonal nod to the hatchet. Acid green and hot pink make a memorable, fashion-forward calling card.

Designed to hold in your hand.

Options 01–06 and 08 are standard US business cards: 3.5 × 2 inches. Option 07 uses the same size turned upright. Artwork is shown at the finished trim edge, with no simulated foil, embossing, or paper texture. All lettering is converted to vector outlines, so the SVG files keep their appearance without installed fonts. The existing emblem and bouquet photograph are embedded images.

These are design proofs. After you choose a direction, the selected card should receive printer-specific bleed, color conversion, and a physical proof. Bright pink and acid green will look softer in ordinary CMYK print; specialty inks can be discussed with the printer. Contact details come from the website: Jeneva, jeneva@daisyhatchet.com, and @daisy_hatchet_flowers. No phone number or street address has been invented.

My starting picks: 01 for the clearest connection to the website, 02 for a quieter personal card, and 07 for a memorable keepsake.

Private local design study · Website unchanged · No production publication
